mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a strong, decelerating-but-positive week-on-week recovery trend (-45.6 to -28.0) over the last four weeks. This momentum reflects an ongoing re-normalization of shopping and recreation activity that should persist, pushing the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -45.6 to -28.0 over last four weeks
failure_condition: If the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean despite continued weekly improvement in the trailing series, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Once PARKS mobility crosses from negative to positive territory, it signals a behavioral substitution where households reallocate discretionary trips toward outdoor leisure instead of retail and recreation venues, dampening RETAIL_REC growth in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -6.0 to 6.1 to 9.1 over last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week immediately following PARKS turning positive, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has plateaued near -36 to -37 for three consecutive weeks, indicating that restriction policy has stabilized rather than tightened. This policy stability removes downside pressure on commuting-linked retail footfall, allowing RETAIL_REC to continue its gradual increase over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held between -37.4 and -35.9 for the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining stable within a 2-point band, the policy-stability hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery of TRANSIT (-52.3 to -36.6) and WORKPLACES (relatively flat) indicates renewed commuting-linked mobility; when both series improve together, the combined effect amplifies incidental retail visits beyond what either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 10 points over two weeks while WORKPLACES does not decline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -52.3 to -36.6 while WORKPLACES stayed near -36 to -37
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT improving and WORKPLACES remaining stable, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained persistently elevated around 7.3-7.4 percent above baseline for three weeks, indicating a saturated level of stay-home behavior that caps the pace at which households resume retail and recreation outings, causing RETAIL_REC growth to decelerate or flatten.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 7.0 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between 7.3 and 7.4 for the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a similar or accelerated pace while RESIDENTIAL remains flat above 7.0, the saturation hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility growth has decelerated sharply, from a 10-point weekly gain to near-zero change in the most recent week, suggesting essential-trip demand has saturated. Since GROCERY_PHARM historically leads RETAIL_REC by about one week in this recovery phase, this deceleration implies RETAIL_REC's own weekly gains will similarly slow in the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM weekly gain fell from 10.0 to 0.1 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's week-on-week gain accelerates rather than decelerates in the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM flattening, the lead-lag hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in PARKS and TRANSIT reflects a broad-based normalization of outdoor and commuting mobility; when both series trend upward together over consecutive weeks, this combined signal indicates a general lifting of mobility restrictions that eventually spills over into increased RETAIL_REC over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -14.6 to 9.1 and TRANSIT rose from -52.3 to -36.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite sustained joint increases in both PARKS and TRANSIT, the normalization-spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains deeply suppressed near -36 percent, indicating that workplace-related restrictions are still substantially in force. In this partial-restriction regime, retail footfall growth is structurally capped because commuting-linked incidental shopping cannot fully recover, limiting RETAIL_REC's upside over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remains between -37.4 and -35.9 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises substantially (more than 5 points) over the next two weeks while WORKPLACES remains below -35, the restriction-cap hypothesis is rejected.
